title_ar: ما مضى و ما يأتي من العلامات
title_en: The Portents That Have Already Come and Those Still to Come
body_ar:
يقول الله تعالى: (هل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة فقد جاء أشراطها) هل أتت هذه الأشراط أم ما زالت منتظرة؟

بعض الأشراط قد أتى و منه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فبعثته شرط من أشراط الساعة "بعثت أنا و الساعة كهاتين"

و هو نبي الساعة و منها كذلك ما بينه من رفع الأمانة و من ظهور الجهل و من كثرة الهرج و هو القتل و من قلة الرجال و كثرة النساء و ما بينه كذلك من قتال المسلمين للترك و ما بينه كذلك من غدر النصارى بالمسلمين فهذه الأمور قد حصلت.

أما الأمور التي ستحصل فمنها الأشراط الكبرى و منها خروج الدجال و نزول المسيح ابن مريم و خروج الداب و رفع القرآن و خسف بالمشرق و خسف بالمغرب و خسف بجزيرة العرب و منها نار تخرج من قعر عدن تسوق الناس إلى المحشر و منها خروج يأجوج و مأجوج و منها نقض الكعبة بعد ذلك فهذه الأشراط الكبرى التي ستأتي.
body_en:
God, exalted, says: {Are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? Its portents have already come} (Sūrat Muḥammad 47:18). Have these portents come, or are they still awaited?

Some of the portents have already come, and among them is the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: his being sent is one of the portents of the Hour — 'I and the Hour were sent like these two.'

He is the Prophet of the Hour. Among them likewise are the things he set out: the lifting away of trust (al-amānah); the coming out of ignorance into the open; the abundance of harj, which is killing; the scarcity of men and the multitude of women; and likewise what he set out about the Muslims fighting the Turks, and what he set out about the treachery of the Christians towards the Muslims. These things have already taken place.

As for the things that are still to happen: among them are the major portents. Among them are the coming out of the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl); the descent of the Messiah, son of Mary; the coming out of the Beast; the lifting away of the Qur'an; a sinking of the earth in the east, a sinking in the west, and a sinking in the Arabian Peninsula; a fire that comes out from the depths of Aden, driving the people to the place of gathering; the coming out of Gog and Magog (Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj); and after that the pulling down of the Kaaba. These are the major portents that are to come.

flags.arabic: قتال المسلمين للترك … غدر النصارى بالمسلمين
flags.context: the list of portents the Sheikh says have already occurred
options: render literally, keeping 'the Turks' and 'the Christians' as the Arabic has them
render with a gloss identifying these as the wordings of specific prophetic reports
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. These two items are the wordings of well-known prophetic reports about the portents of the Hour, and the Sheikh reproduces them as such without further comment. Read in English out of that frame, a sentence naming an ethnic group and a religious community as the subject of predicted conflict and treachery carries clear reputational risk. It has been translated faithfully and neither softened nor strengthened; the decision on whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. Note that the Sheikh gives no narrator, no collection and no grading for any of these reports, and none has been supplied.

flags.context: the list of major portents still to come
options: leave the source spelling visible and render as 'the Beast', flagging the defect
silently read الدابة and render 'the Beast'
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The source reads الداب, which is not a word; the intended reading is plainly الدابة, 'the Beast' (Sūrat al-Naml 27:82). The defective spelling is preserved in body_ar per the house rule against silently fixing the source, and the English gives the evident sense. Flagged so a reviewer can confirm rather than a translator assume.

flags.context: the report quoted for the Prophet's mission being a portent of the Hour
options: quote as the Sheikh gives it, with no attribution or grading
flags.note: The Sheikh quotes this report without narrator, collection or grading, and none has been supplied, per the house rule. The gesture that accompanies the saying — the two fingers held together — is not described in this record, which leaves the English slightly opaque; a reviewer may wish to decide whether the site supplies that context editorially.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The Qur'anic quotation is given in the source in round brackets and without a reference; the reference has been supplied in the English per house style. The wording matches Sūrat Muḥammad 47:18.

'The lifting away of trust' renders rafʿ al-amānah, and 'the lifting away of the Qur'an' renders rafʿ al-Qurʾān; both are the technical eschatological idiom of the reports, not a general figure of speech.
harj has been kept in transliteration with the Sheikh's own gloss ('which is killing') following it, because the gloss is his and not the translator's.
